Subject: Re: sudden p95 spikes in gen-api (QuickCart production)

Hey Aditya / Marissa —

We're seeing sustained P95 jumps from ~320ms to ~1.2s for our gen-api calls starting around 07:45 PT. Error rate is low (~0.2%) but latency is spiky and blocking some checkout flows during peak (07:30–08:30). Our ops team attached a short token-level dump and an aggregated trace we captured.

Can you confirm whether this is related to any rollout or infra change on your side? This started immediately after your 07:40 model routing deploy. QuickCart is impacted (we're in the middle of a marketing push) — we need ETA on mitigation and a customer-facing note.

Attachments: token_dump_2027-08-16.csv (csv), network-trace-0816.txt (txt)

Subject: Re: sudden p95 spikes in gen-api (QuickCart production)

Aditya / team — quick triage notes below. I'm attaching the shorttrace files from our side and referencing the customer dump.

What I'm seeing:
- Timeline aligns with the 07:40 routing config change.
- Root candidate: a cache eviction pattern on the shared prefix cache after the routing update. QuickCart's traffic has many long-tail prefixes, and a transient eviction caused repeated first-token recompute for some hot requests. That spikes tail latency rather than increasing error rate.
- Secondary: a small CPU scheduling jitter on the Dedicated pool serving QuickCart (we saw a brief NPU reclaim that increased kernel latency for ~2 minutes).

Immediate mitigations I can apply now (risk low):
1) Temporarily pin QuickCart traffic to the older dedicated pool we ran last week (no model changes) — expected p95 reduction within 2–4m.
2) Increase prefix cache size for QuickCart tenant from 256MB -> 1GB (will reduce eviction but uses more RAM).
3) Enable short-term conservative batching (smaller max batch) for QuickCart to reduce tail compaction.

I'll start with option 1 (pin traffic) and option 2 in parallel if we still see elevated tail. If we pin, we should notify QuickCart immediately; it's a non-invasive operator change.

Attachments: engine_short_trace_0816.txt

—Dylan
Senior SRE
Redwood Inference

Subject: QuickCart — short service update (P95 spike observed, mitigation in progress)

Hi Nina / QuickCart ops team,

We observed elevated P95 latency for gen-api calls starting at ~07:45 PT. Our SREs have identified a routing-related cache eviction increase following a routine routing configuration change and are applying a low-risk failover now. Expected impact: reduced p95 within minutes.

What we're doing now:
- Pinning traffic to the prior dedicated pool (no model changes) to restore stable tail latency.
- Increasing per-tenant cache allocation while we validate the fix.

Next steps and ask from you:
- We'll confirm when P95 returns to baseline and provide the post-mortem.
- If you prefer we can schedule a short call to walk through the mitigations.

We understand the timing is unfortunate. We'll follow up with a root-cause write-up and any recommended guardrails to prevent recurrence.

—Marissa
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

All — quick summary and action items after the initial fixes: pin + cache bump applied at 09:00 PT; QuickCart confirmed p95 returned to baseline by ~09:06. Good work.

Action items (owners + timelines):
- Dylan: open a post-incident Jira with traces and exact config diff (due EOD today). Please include the temporary routing change ID and the cache sizing delta.
- Karthik: product decision — prioritize a per-tenant cache autoscale / eviction-smoothing feature on the roadmap. Can you draft a short PRD and proposed priority? Link it to the incident runbook: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3cQC-incident-runbook (please add estimated dev effort).
- Marissa: finalize and send the customer-facing note (approved copy below). Offer QuickCart a one-week elevated support window and ask if they'd like a review call.
- Aditya: I'll coordinate SLA credit if needed and confirm with finance.

Customer note (final):
Hi Nina —

Thanks again for the quick signal and traces. We identified a routing-related cache eviction pattern after a routine routing update; our SREs applied a targeted failover and cache sizing increase that restored baseline tail latency within ~6 minutes. We're filing a full post-mortem and will share mitigation guardrails. We are also accelerating a product change to make per-tenant cache sizing more robust.

Would you like a 30-minute follow-up call later today or tomorrow?

—Aditya on behalf of Redwood Inference

I'll follow up separately with the Jira and the PRD link. Good recovery all around.

Aditya Rao
